node.title: Global fixed-mu order for max common-terminal relay roots
node.statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, fixed mu>1, and the max relay law, the oriented relay IVP is uniquely defined with finitely many switches on every compact time interval for every q>1 and depends continuously on q across all material chambers and compatible closures. The indexed common-terminal residual A_n(mu,q) is one globally continuous function; each of its zeros is automatically a premise-complete transverse 2n-event root and has the global derivative partial_q A_n>0. Consequently A_n(mu,.) has at most one zero on q>1, and every max common-terminal root is reflection fixed. This theorem asserts neither existence for each mu nor uniqueness of the equal-integral residual in mu, and it does not establish max O3a.

ordered_steps: For the oriented max relay IVP at arbitrary q>1, derive the conserved energy E=P^2-Q^2=1-q^2<0 on every material cell and across every switch.

At a nonjoint switch zero S=0, a grazing derivative would force P=epsilon mu Q and hence E=(mu^2-1)Q^2>=0, a contradiction. At a joint zero U=V=0, the energy inequalities make S strictly negative on both punctured sides, so the point is an isolated quadratic negative contact and not an active material switch.

Construct the relay trajectory successively through transverse events. Any finite event accumulation would limit to a forbidden nonjoint grazing or to a joint contact having a punctured negative neighborhood, so Zeno switching is impossible; a.e.-labelled global uniqueness follows on every compact interval.

Use uniform energy bounds, Arzela-Ascoli compactness, and the Volterra form of the equations to prove continuous dependence on q even when a vanishing event pair is born or dies. Indexed simple scalar zero times therefore remain continuous, and A_n(mu,q)=T_U^n-T_V^(n+1) is one global continuous function on q>1 rather than disconnected chamber formulas.

At every zero A_n=0, strict Wronskian-ratio monotonicity between consecutive scalar zeros gives the accepted consecutive n and n+1 nodal allocation, exactly 2n simple relay events, and negative endpoint cells. Thus every global zero is automatically a premise-complete transverse common-terminal root in the R8 local-twist scope.

Near a terminal joint contact, compare the true relay to the frozen negative-material continuation. A quadratic upper bound confines every possible material discrepancy to a window of width O(|delta q|); within that window the position amplitudes are O(|delta q|), so acceleration mismatch is O(|delta q|), velocity mismatch is O(delta q^2), and position mismatch is O(delta q^3). The two fixed-chamber implicit zero times move by O(|delta q|), while nonzero terminal slopes convert the true-versus-frozen position mismatch into an O(delta q^2) indexed zero-time error.

The terminal softness estimate proves that the R8 chamber derivative is also the derivative of the single global residual at every zero, including closure zeros, and hence every zero is strictly positively oriented.

A continuous real function on an interval that is differentiable with positive derivative at every zero cannot have two zeros: two distinct zeros would require a last positive-to-nonpositive transition with nonpositive local orientation. Therefore A_n(mu,.) has at most one q>1 root. Reflection covariance produces another root at the same mu; uniqueness identifies it with the original root and relay-IVP uniqueness gives reflection invariance.
boundary_cases: Covers n=2 and every n>=2, arbitrary finite R>1, fixed mu>1, and all q>1 for the max law; the theorem is not asserted for the min law.

Nonjoint grazing is excluded by strict negative energy. Joint zeros, including a common terminal zero, are retained as isolated negative quadratic contacts rather than incorrectly treated as transverse switches.

Material chamber boundaries, event-pair birth or death, and asymmetric roots are covered; the terminal softness estimate explicitly handles the only closure where the material word changes at first sight.
R=1, mu=1, q=1, infinite time, and nonphysical initial data are outside the theorem. No existence statement for a root at each mu is made.
The reflection conclusion is derived after global fixed-mu uniqueness and is not used as a premise.
Equal-integral orientation in mu, possible disconnected mu-domains, min complementary inertia, and universal O3a remain unresolved. No finite computation enters the proof.

math_research_state_records.status_justification: The exact R9 relay-continuity and terminal-softness theorem combines with the trusted R8 local positive twist to prove at most one max common-terminal q root for every fixed mu across all chambers and compatible closures.

Fixed-mu q uniqueness leaves the mu direction and the equal-integral residual unoriented. The natural mu tangent has unequal component Wronskians and is not controlled by the R8 positive path form, so a full residual-Jacobian or equivalent shape-Hessian sign remains open.
The route rigorously closes global fixed-mu max root order and reflection fixing, while equal-norm orientation, all min-sign gaps, and universal O3a remain open.
